title: Why is Yujiro Hanma nicknamed "The Ogre"?
summary: Scripted essay on Yujiro Hanma's 'Ogre' nickname in Baki, tying it to European ogre folklore, Cronus devouring his sons, and the ogre as a symbol of adversity and natural selection. Contrasts the naturally monstrous Yujiro with Jack, who needed drugs and surgery.
claims: Ogres in folklore are hyper-muscular man-eating humanoids that personified mass violence, war and parents' fear of losing children; the nickname casts Yujiro as that archetype
Folk ogres are defeated by brains rather than brawn, and Yujiro likewise can only be survived through avoidance or strategy, never direct confrontation
Jack Hanma is no genuine ogre because he used drugs and surgery to build his body, so he never matched his natural-born father; banking everything on strength alone fails against ogres
Yujiro mirrors the titan Cronus devouring his sons, and Baki's mother sacrificing herself echoes Rhea hiding Zeus
Yujiro's feline features, mane of hair, darker skin and appetite for 20 people match classical ogre descriptions
The ogre represents adversity and a great filter; a boy becomes a man when he no longer fears the difficulties of the world
Attempts to destroy the ogre only multiply violence, because the ferocity it represents cannot disappear
